### Loop 4 — 2026-10-09 · H1/H2
- **D-H1a — preview server is allow-list only.** scripts/workspace_server.py serves: `/` (generated homepage), gabriel_homes/{templates,static,docs}/ (browsable), gabriel_homes/{DEPLOY.md, DESIGN.md, WORK.md, requirements.txt, README*}, scripts/preview_site/{index,plan,checklist,qa}.html. Everything else → 403. A hard deny-list (any dot-file component, .env*, *.sqlite3, *.db, *.log, *.pyc, cookies.txt, __pycache__, download/, upload/, node_modules/, media/) runs independently of the allow-list so future allow-list edits can never leak those paths. Rationale: this server fronts a public preview link; earlier ad-hoc servers either showed only preview_site or had no principled boundary at all.
- **D-H1b — scripts/ reachable only for the four preview pages + assets.** The four HTML pages are the owner-facing purpose of the server; the rest of scripts/ is agent tooling (code, logs, cookies, scratch dirs) with real leak value and no preview value. scripts/preview_site/qa-shots/*.png is served ONLY because qa.html embeds it (the QA page renders broken otherwise); the qa-shots folder itself stays unlistable (403). Enforced in code, not config.
- **D-H2 — two export zips, two policies.** (1) gabriel-homes-oneclick.zip (customer deliverable) intentionally ships the seeded demo db.sqlite3 so the first run skips seeding; it now EXCLUDES .git/ and real .env (rsync previously leaked the whole repo history) and asserts .env.example/.gitignore/docs in staging and inside the finished archive. (2) gabriel-workspace-snapshot.zip (owner workspace export) must contain gabriel_homes/.env.example, .gitignore, docs/STATUS.md, docs/AGENT-BRIEF.md, manage.py and must NEVER contain db.sqlite3, download/, upload/, scripts/server.log — scripts/check_export.sh exits 1 and names each violation. unzip -Z1 (zipinfo names mode) is used instead of parsing unzip -l columns: same tool, exact filenames, no whitespace parsing.

### Loop 5 — 2026-10-09 · H3/H4/H6
- **D-H3 · pytest-cov==7.1.0 pinned as a dev/test dependency.** The G-COV gate stage needs pytest-cov; it previously existed only in the agent's venv, so a fresh environment failed the gate at `coverage` (reproduced RED in /tmp/h3venv via gate.sh's PYTHON switch). It belongs in the "Dev / test only" block: gunicorn/prod never imports it, pytest is already there. 7.1.0 is the PyPI latest and verified compatible with pytest==9.0.3 (fresh-venv gate GREEN after the pin).
- **D-H4 · snapshot builder interface.** build_workspace_snapshot.sh now takes WS_ROOT from the environment (default = the directory two levels above the script itself — portable, no /home hard-coding) and the output path as argument 1 (default $WS_ROOT/download/gabriel-workspace-snapshot.zip). The reported file count is read back from the finished zip (zipfile namelist), never from a walk pre-count — the pre-count could print "0 files" while the zip was fine. Regression-covered by scripts/tests_build_snapshot.sh (fake workspace, planted leaks, H4MARKER.txt to prove WS_ROOT is honored).
- **D-H6 · placeholder rule for the DEPLOY.md doc-lint.** scripts/tests_deploy_doc.py enumerates every angle-bracket placeholder it finds (<REPO_URL>, <generated-50+-char-key>, <release-tag>, <repo-url>) as "ALLOWED PLACEHOLDERS" on every run. Placeholders neither satisfy a check silently nor get auto-replaced by the agent; they stay visible until Brian fills them. The test parses `manage.py help --commands` as ground truth for command names, env-var assignments/shell refs vs .env.example, and verifies scripts/*.sh|py references exist (including "$SRC/scripts/..." forms).

### Loop 14 — 2026-11-01 · Owner tree merge + detail map completion (D-MAP-DET)
- **D-MAP-DET · The property detail map joins the search map on self-hosted MapLibre GL + OpenFreeMap positron — the OSM iframe embed is gone.** The Codex tree shipped the detail page with an openstreetmap.org/export iframe plus an orphaned MapLibre detail-map.js (its #detail-map target WAS the iframe, and the script tag had been removed leaving an empty {% if %} stub — unfinished work). Finishing the GL version wins over keeping the iframe: one rendering stack for both maps, one vendoring convention, no external frame dependency (openstreetmap.org availability/rate limits), no frame-src carve-out in the CSP, and the same graceful-degradation story. The outbound "Open in OpenStreetMap" link stays — it is an <a>, not a frame. CSS: the dead Leaflet control rules became MapLibre theming; #detail-map keeps its 400px height; loading/error fallback text styled inside the container. static/vendor/leaflet/ (396K) now has zero code references — left on disk for a deliberate future cleanup rather than silently deleted (S10's vendoring decisions live in this file, so removal should too).
- **D-MAP-RST · "Show all homes" reset pill restored on the search map.** The Codex rewrite of search-map.js dropped the reset the redesign had; with fitBounds-on-load only, a visitor who pans into one neighbourhood had no way back. The pill is created in JS (CSP-clean, no inline handlers), overlays the stage top-left, calls the same fitBounds as the initial frame, and is hidden until more than one pin exists (a single-pin map starts perfectly framed).
- **D-CSP-FRAME · frame-src removed from the CSP.** With the detail iframe gone the site frames nothing at all (verified live: zero <iframe> elements on every smoke page), so the policy reverts to frame-ancestors 'none' only. Tiles stay single-host: tiles.openfreemap.org in img-src + connect-src, worker same-origin/blob per the MapLibre ESM worker. Pinned by the rewritten test_csp_allows_map_tile_hosts_only.
- **D-VENDOR-SRI · No SRI integrity attributes on the vendored MapLibre ESM module.** Dynamic import() (the mechanism both maps use via data-maplibre-src) does not honour SRI — a hash on the tag would be security theatre. The files are same-origin under script-src 'self'; the real guards are the vendoring hygiene test (no sourceMappingURL → collectstatic survives — both .mjs bundles were stripped this run) and the vendor-files-on-disk test. If the module ever moves back to a plain <script> tag, pin SRI then (r13's approach).
- **D-MERGE-14 · The owner's Codex tree is the lineage of record.** Two parallel trees existed after run 13 (the r12/r13 tree and the owner's Codex tree). The Codex tree won on recency (freshest dev DB, lead-listing gallery + video, demo nearby amenities) and on the map implementation (one renderer instead of Leaflet+bridge). The r12 hardening was ported in wholesale rather than rebased, and the LOOP records (STATE, BRIEF §14, this file) now tell both lineages honestly: run 13's approach is documented as superseded, not erased.

### Loop 16 — 2026-11-05 · F2 capability gate shipped (D-LOOP-16)
- **D-LOOP-16a · fx-gate.js is the single capability decision point.** One tiny deferred script sets `html[data-fx]` ∈ {rich, lite, none} (reduced-motion ⇒ none; Save-Data / ≤4 cores / ≤4 GB ⇒ lite; else rich) and `html[data-fine]` on (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). motion.js and bento-shift.js no longer check prefers-reduced-motion or pointer media queries themselves — a pytest guard pins fx-gate.js as the ONLY JS file allowed to mention prefers-reduced-motion. CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion) token blocks stay: they zero out transition durations (CSS parity layer), they make no decisions.
- **D-LOOP-16b · Fail-closed both ways.** With JavaScript blocked the gate never runs, no attribute exists, and no effect script activates (D-MOTION-SAFE unchanged: reveal CSS still only under html.motion-ready). If fx-gate.js itself is blocked/stale, motion.js and bento-shift.js read the missing data-fx as "none" — effects off, content fully visible. base.html loads the gate OUTSIDE {% block scripts %} so child templates (all call {{ block.super }}) can never drop it; the <html> tag must never hardcode data-fx (guard test).
- **D-LOOP-16c · Bento shape-shift is now rich-tier + fine-pointer only, and under fx=none it does not run at all.** Today's reduced-motion path still promoted the hovered card with an instant (unanimated) layout change; the runbook's "no effect runs under none" cuts that too — under none the grid behaves exactly like a touch device (plain cards, no promotion, no reflow). lite devices (Save-Data / ≤4 cores / ≤4 GB) also skip it. The viewport half of the old check (min-width 1021px) stays local to bento-shift.js — it is layout, not capability, and H3 builds on it.

### Loop 17 — 2026-11-05 · F2 audited MET-T1 + F1 token integrity shipped (D-LOOP-17)
- **D-LOOP-17a · `--paper` is single-sourced in tokens.css at exactly `#f3eee6`.** The token was undefined; its two usages (`.listing-row__facts span`, `.band-soft`) carried inline fallbacks `#f3eee6`, which is treated as the intended value — so defining it there is a zero-visual-delta fix. The inline fallbacks are removed (single source of truth) and a test pins the value: changing `--paper` now requires a DECISIONS entry, not a drive-by.
- **D-LOOP-17b · The F1 undefined-var scan counts template inline styles and JS `setProperty('--x', …)` as legitimate definition sources.** home.html's per-section `style="--bg: url('…')"` photo pattern is an intentional dynamic custom property, not a broken var; only vars with no definition anywhere AND no fallback fail (exactly one real offender existed: `var(--font-body)` in the map price pin — the r13-era suspicion confirmed; it silently invalidated the pin's font declaration. Now `var(--font-sans)`).
- **D-LOOP-17c · The 13px floor is enforced as a documented allowlist + two ratchets, recorded at r17.** Sub-13px px font sizes are allowed only for the 12 (file, px) pairs in `test_f1_token_integrity.py::FONT_FLOOR_ALLOWLIST` (map/attribution overlays, uppercase-mono eyebrow micro type, staff dashboard labels — each with a reason; mirrored in a tokens.css comment). Baselines at r17: sub-floor total 44, hard-coded hex outside tokens.css 240 — both may only go DOWN (the hex count already dropped to 238 with the `--paper` fallback removal). Counting rules are documented in the test docstring so future runs can recompute identical numbers.

### Loop 19 — 2026-11-05 · H1 audited MET-T1 + H3 mobile bento shipped (D-LOOP-19)
- **D-LOOP-19a · The mobile bento carousel is pure CSS and degrades by design.** Under 1021px `.bento-grid--shift` becomes a flex scroll-snap rail (cards 82% wide, spotlight 88%, `scroll-snap-align: center`, clamp() height, hidden scrollbar). The centre-card scale-up runs as a scroll-driven `animation-timeline: view(inline)` animation (0.92 → 1) behind `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` — browsers without scroll-driven animations show an equal-scale snap rail that still swipes, still snaps and still works keyboard-only (browsers scroll the focused card into view) and with JS blocked. `bento-shift.js` and every >1020px desktop rule are untouched (grep-guarded by test_h3_mobile_bento.py); reduced-motion sets `animation: none` on the cards. No JS was added — the carousel cannot break the FX gate contract.
